title: Open Profiling Dataset — Case Record
description: Schema for a case that does NOT meet the offender-roster inclusion criteria but is analytically valuable: no homicide conviction, contested confession, exoneration, unidentified offender, or a conviction resting on discredited forensics. Where a profile records what an offender did, a case record documents the GAP between what is publicly claimed and what is judicially established. That gap is the object of study. These records are never counted in offender aggregates.

tier.description: 1 = primary record. 2 = peer-reviewed. 3 = book-length journalism with a sourcing apparatus. 4 = contemporaneous reporting. Dramatisations, unsourced podcasts, wikis and AI-generated text are NOT admissible at any tier.

search_exhausted.description: For 'unverified' claims only, and required on them. TRUE = the absence is a finding (searched properly, or null by design). FALSE = the absence is a todo. See schema/profile.schema.json for the full rationale.

id.description: Same identifier form as profiles. A subject may hold an id in index/cases.csv OR index/roster.csv, never both.

case_type.description: Why this is a case record rather than an offender profile. 'exonerated' subjects are never described as offenders in any field.

exclusion_rationale.description: Why this subject is not on the offender roster. Mandatory and public: an exclusion nobody can audit is worthless.

criteria_failed.description: Which numbered criteria in docs/inclusion-criteria.md this case fails.

not_an_exoneration.description: Set true where the subject stands convicted of something and exclusion must not be read as a claim of innocence. Rendered as a prominent warning.

judicial_status.description: State precisely what the subject stands convicted of, if anything. This is the field the whole record exists to get right.

established.description: What the record DOES support. Convictions, judicial findings, physical evidence, forensic determinations.

judicial_findings.description: Findings a court actually made — including findings against the prosecution.

cause_of_death_determination.description: Whether a cause of death was established at all. In several cases it was not, which is decisive and routinely omitted from popular accounts.

not_established.description: The core of this schema. What is widely asserted but NOT supported — stated plainly, with the source of the assertion identified. Do not soften: if a figure has no provenance, say it has no provenance.

homicide_attribution.description: Deaths attributed to the subject without charge or conviction. Name who attributed, on what basis.

victim_count_claims.description: Circulating totals and where each originates. Never recorded as a count.

circulating_claims.description: Widely repeated specifics with no evidentiary basis — including details originating in dramatisations. Naming them here is how the record inoculates readers against them.

confession_record.description: For cases turning on admissions. The circumstances of a confession determine its evidentiary weight; record them, not just its existence.

circumstances.description: Duration, number of sessions, whether recorded, who wrote the statement, what inducements existed.

corroboration.description: What independent evidence, if any, confirmed the admissions. 'None located' is a finding.

reliability_findings.description: What courts or examining experts concluded about reliability.

other_suspects.description: Alternative suspects raised in the proceedings. Name them ONLY where already named in the public court record, never on the strength of speculation.

research_value.description: Why this case is in the dataset at all. A case record with no stated analytic use is just an accusation with citations.
